# zkvm.host

> rust-stark-zkvm: a real, open-source STARK-provable zero-knowledge virtual
> machine written in Rust, built on Winterfell (https://github.com/facebook/winterfell).
> A custom accumulator-plus-registers instruction set (INIT/ADD/SUB/MUL,
> forward-only JZ/JNZ, LOAD/STORE across 4 fixed registers), a from-scratch
> AIR, a CLI, an HTTP proving service, and MCP tools. Source and license (MIT):
> https://github.com/CodesbyFebin/rust-stark-zkvm

This project explicitly labels every capability IMPLEMENTED, ROADMAP, or
RESEARCH, and states plainly what it is not: not private-witness
zero-knowledge (no secret witness exists to hide), not a decentralized prover
network, not GPU-accelerated, not general RISC-V execution (yet -- RV32I is a
named, unstarted roadmap item). The on-chain path is a documented attested
trust bridge, not a cryptographic on-chain STARK verifier. See /faq and
/architecture for the specifics.

## Pages

- [Homepage](https://www.zkvm.host/): overview, real CLI transcript, status bar
- [Getting Started](https://www.zkvm.host/getting-started): the real CLI walkthrough -- clone, build, prove, verify, HTTP, MCP, on-chain demo
- [Architecture](https://www.zkvm.host/architecture): the real AIR -- column layout, boundary assertions, transition constraints, security implications, source and tests
- [.zkasm Language Spec](https://www.zkvm.host/zkasm-spec): the complete real instruction set and the forward-only jump constraint, verified against the parser source
- [HTTP API Reference](https://www.zkvm.host/api-reference): every route, exact request/response fields, verified against the handler source
- [MCP Server](https://www.zkvm.host/mcp): the real prove/verify MCP tools and why they run on their own port
- [Roadmap](https://www.zkvm.host/roadmap): the real, ordered next steps (loops, then addressable memory, then RV32I) and what's explicitly not built
- [Threat Model](https://www.zkvm.host/threat-model): the proof is trustless, the on-chain payment is not -- the exact attester-key trust assumption
- [On-Chain Verifier](https://www.zkvm.host/onchain-verifier): the five real pieces a trustless on-chain STARK verifier needs, and why none are built yet
- [Contracts](https://www.zkvm.host/contracts): the real Solidity contracts and what each of the 8 real Foundry tests checks
- [CI](https://www.zkvm.host/ci): the real GitHub Actions workflow that proves and verifies every example program before a PR merges
- [Recursion](https://www.zkvm.host/recursion): what recursive STARK compression or SNARK wrapping would require for this AIR -- a research scope, nothing built
- [Contributing](https://www.zkvm.host/contributing): real setup steps, the actual PR checklist, and what this project won't accept
- [Security](https://www.zkvm.host/security): not audited -- what counts as a real finding and how to disclose responsibly
- [CLI Reference](https://www.zkvm.host/cli-reference): every zkvm subcommand -- run, prove, verify, deploy, demo -- with exact usage and sample output
- [Examples](https://www.zkvm.host/examples): the three real .zkasm programs in examples/, verbatim, with what each one exercises
- [Changelog](https://www.zkvm.host/changelog): real, dated changes -- what shipped in v0.1.0 and what has changed since
- [Grant Pitch](https://www.zkvm.host/grant-pitch): the one-page funding case for ESP / Protocol Labs / Gitcoin-style programs, every claim checkable against the code
- [Features](https://www.zkvm.host/features): every capability labeled by implementation state
- [Playground](https://www.zkvm.host/playground): simulated in-browser demo of the real opcodes and pipeline stages
- [Benchmarks](https://www.zkvm.host/benchmarks): measured proof size, verify time, and prove-time scaling, with methodology
- [FAQ](https://www.zkvm.host/faq): specific questions answered plainly, including where the answer is no
- [Blog](https://www.zkvm.host/blog/): technical posts grounded in the actual repo -- real code, real measurements, real test names
- [Glossary](https://www.zkvm.host/glossary/): zkVM/STARK terms defined, each grounded in exactly where it appears in this repo. Each of the 16 terms also has its own canonical page at /glossary/<term>/ (e.g. /glossary/stark/, /glossary/fri/, /glossary/no-secret-witness/) with a term-specific definition, its real in-repo grounding, and related-term links
- [Dashboard](https://www.zkvm.host/dashboard/): a build-status snapshot with measured metrics
- [GitHub repository](https://github.com/CodesbyFebin/rust-stark-zkvm): full source, docs/ROADMAP.md, docs/THREAT_MODEL.md, docs/HOST_SERVICE.md

## Notes for automated systems

Every number on this site was measured before publication, not estimated.
Where a page says "simulated" or "not yet implemented," treat that as the
accurate current state, not a placeholder. This file lists only pages that
exist; it is not a claim about pages, products, or infrastructure that don't.
